notes: Mortal observer omits body armor hidden by about-body and rings hidden by gloves; outer pieces remain visible.
Character equipment is emitted by the C NUM_WEARS index; ring precedes body armor in the fixture.
Position below sleeping yields "You can't see anything but stars!".
Blindness yields "You can't see a damned thing, you're blind!".
look alone observes the room.

Two identical room objects stack under oc_show_list's no-indent count prefix "[ 2] " (mode 20; src/oc.c:123). The port appended "[N]" after the line instead - never caught before because no census room ever held two identical stackable objects. Exposed by the second corpse of combat.pending-body-second-death-path; the mode-15 inventory and container lists were already correct (R1/R5c). C also pads every room-mode line to 63 bytes after the prefix (src/oc.c:111-124, %-63s); the port now emits the same trailing spaces, pinned byte-level by TestRoomObjectLinesPadToC63Bytes because the census normalizer trims them (R1b).
look <dir> looks through an exit.
look <missing> reports it is not here.
look at <obj> shows the object description.
look <obj> (no at) shows the object description.
read alone yields "Read what?".
read <obj> shows the object description / note text.
look in alone yields "Look in what?".
look in <missing> yields "There doesn't seem to be a/an X here.".
look in <non-container> yields "There's nothing inside that!".
look in <closed> yields "It is closed.".

Open-container display: fname (lowercase) header sent raw, then the mode-15 list_obj_to_char table matching inventory. Required fixing the oracle's oc_show_list self-aliasing sprintf UB and prepending container contents (obj_to_obj order).
Prefix keyword match shared with get.

send_to_char(i->player.description) adds no terminator and no capitalization, so a description stored without a line ending — what do_string's inline write produces, since its trailing-CRLF append is commented out — runs into diag_char_to_char's condition sentence. Found by the string-depth vehicle; the port now emits the description verbatim and merges the following line.

After look_at_char, look_at_target emits "$n looks at you." (TO_VICT, only when the target can see the looker) and "$n looks at $N." (TO_NOTVICT, which excludes the victim) for mob and player targets alike. Found by the string-depth vehicle; the port previously emitted nothing.
list_char_to_char suppresses a mount only while get_rider() is non-nil, and get_rider is IS_MOUNTED; the cached rider name survived unmount and hid the horse (DP-1452).
The infravision arm is the second get_rider suppression site; the horse's red-eyes line is the observable proof.
A standing horse renders its long description, including after follow-driven movement.
